title: Staggered Occupancy: Adaptive Tile + KV Snapshot Strategy for Bursty Inference
content:
Goal / elevator pitch:
Try to reduce tail latency for bursty small requests without sacrificing throughput for long sequences. Combine an occupancy-aware kernel tiling strategy with lightweight, consistent KV 'snapshots' so paged KV and FlashAttention-style fusion can coexist without global locks or expensive migrations.

Context / why this came up:
- Observed production spikes where short-chat requests (<= 64 tokens) suffer tail latency when long-context requests (>= 2048) cause uneven GPU occupancy and thrashing of the paged KV layer.
- Current heuristics either degrade throughput (conservative tiling) or cause hot-page churn (aggressive contiguous allocation).
- Need a design that: (1) adapts kernel tile size based on instantaneous occupancy; (2) maintains KV page consistency for in-flight slices; (3) allows FlashAttention-like fused kernels to run with partial KV availability.

High level approach:
1) Staggered occupancy windows: split the GPU warp/CTA launch plan into micro-windows that bias for small-token requests to run on lightly-loaded SMs while grouping long requests into wider-tiling launches.
2) Adaptive tile widths: tile width (W) is selected per-launch based on an occupancy-advisor metric (see below). W controls shared-memory allocation for attention tiles and influences per-request memory footprints.
3) KV snapshotting: when a request is preempted or migrates between tiling granularities, we create a tiny immutable "page snapshot" for the KV deltas required by the resumed kernel. The snapshot is a compact packed diff (token ranges + delta pointers) that makes paged-KV eviction simpler and avoids in-place rewrites.
4) Seamless fusion: fused FlashAttention kernels will accept either (a) a direct KV pointer for contiguous pages or (b) a snapshot handle that the runtime will resolve to a temporary view. Kernel code paths remain mostly identical; resolution cost is amortized across the batch.

Occupancy advisor (producer of W):
- Inputs: active_request_mix histogram (by sequence-length buckets), SM free registers, shared memory pressure, recent kernel latency tail percentiles (p95,p99).
- Simple scoring: score_W = alpha * (1 / avg_seq_len_bucket) + beta * (free_SM_slots / total_SM) - gamma * (p99_tail_normalized). Normalize and clamp W in [min_W, max_W].
- Implementation: lightweight eBPF-like collector on host + per-GPU sliding window sampler. Runs every 8ms (configurable).

KV snapshot format (compact, delta-oriented):
- header: {request_id, base_generation, token_range_start, token_range_end, flags}  (note: this is conceptual; actual on-GPU structure is packed u32/u64 fields)
- entries: (relative_token_index, compressed_delta_ptr)  -- pointers reference a small arena used for snapshots
- snapshot arena: contiguous GPU memory region allocated per-launch with bump allocator; reclaimed after all kernels referencing snapshot complete.

Kernel handshake protocol (runtime <-> kernel):
- Before launch: runtime computes W, attempts fast-path resolve of KV pointers for batch (all pages contiguous -> fast-path).
- If fast-path fails for some requests, runtime attaches snapshot handles to launch params and marks those lanes as "snapshot_resolve_required".
- Kernel entry sequence (pseudocode):
  lane_id = threadIdx.x / LANE_WIDTH;
  if lane_has_snapshot(handle):
    resolve_snapshot_into_registers(handle);
  else:
    use_direct_kv_pointer();
  run_fused_attention_tile(W);
  if produced_snapshot_delta():
    atomically_publish_delta_to_snapshot_arena();
Tradeoffs / microbench expectations:
- Latency: small requests should see p99 drop by 15-35% depending on mix (sim data shows ~22% on median mixes).
- Throughput: small regression (~3-6%) for full-GPU saturating long-sequence workloads due to staggered windows and occasional snapshot resolve.
- Memory: snapshot arena adds ~2-8% additional working set on peak. However snapshots are transient and reclaimed quickly.

Prototype notes / implementation plan:
1) Host-side occupancy advisor daemon (C++), expose API to serving runtime.
2) Kernel API changes: a minimal extra launch parameter buffer with per-lane handles (u64). Kernel header library that decodes handle and selects path.
3) Snapshot arena allocator (CUDA allocator backed by pinned host memory on fallback) with simple atomic bump + epoch-based reclamation.
4) Integrate with current paged-KV eviction path: when eviction would evict a page with active snapshots, convert in-place page to read-only base + pending-snapshot-list (small vector). Eviction defers actual free until snapshots drained.

Pseudocode for occupancy advisor (host):
- collect_stats_every(8ms):
    seq_hist = histogram(active_requests.seq_len, buckets=[0-32,33-128,129-512,513-2048,>2048])
    free_sm = query_gpu_free_sm_slots()
    p99 = recent_kernel_p99_for_gpu()
    score_inv = 1 / max(1, weighted_mean(seq_hist))
    W = clamp(round(A*score_inv + B*(free_sm/total_sm) - C*p99), min_W, max_W)
    publish_W_for_next_launch(W)

Edge cases and unresolved questions:
- Snapshot size blowup: pathological prompts that produce huge KV diffs (long context append combined with many short inferences) could make snapshot arena large. Mitigation: snapshot thresholding (fall back to conservative eviction if diff > threshold) and early compaction.
- GPU fragmentation: frequent small snapshot allocations could fragment device memory. Consider per-SM arenas or using a pooling strategy keyed by W and sequence class.
- Consistency semantics with rollbacks: if a resumed request is rolled back (model path change), snapshot deltas must be reversible. Option: store reverse patches in snapshot metadata, but increases cost.
- Debugging and visibility: need inspector hooks to show active snapshots, arena usage, and per-request resolve latency in Redwood Console.

Short notes from last sync (2024-05-22):
- Diego: suggested using 16-bit compressed pointers in snapshot entries to reduce header cost; good win for short-runs.
- Aisha: requested that snapshot arena support host-visible mapping for offline postmortem dumps.
- Connor: wants a stress test harness that simulates mixed chat and long-run loads using captured traffic traces.

Next steps / milestones:
- M0 (2 weeks): occupancy advisor + publish-only W; no snapshot path. Measure effect of staggered W on kernels using current KV pointer semantics.
- M1 (4 weeks): implement snapshot arena + kernel handle path for read-only snapshots; integrate with eviction (no writeback path yet).
- M2 (6 weeks): add snapshot delta publish + compaction + dashboard metrics and safety thresholds.
- M3 (8+ weeks): safety rollout on canary cluster, monitor p99 and memory; iterate heuristics.

Quick todo list (who/when):
- Maya: prototype occupancy advisor + simple simulator (due 2024-05-30)
- Diego: microkernel header for snapshot handle decoding (due 2024-06-07)
- Aisha: add snapshot instrumentation to paged-KV eviction flow (due 2024-06-10)
- Connor: assemble synthetic load harness + replay traces (due 2024-06-14)

Notes-to-self / brainstorming fragments:
- Could blend with prefetch cohorts: small requests that repeatedly hit same recent tokens could be grouped into "warm lanes" and kept on SM-local mini-caches.
- Consider an LRU within snapshot arena to compact multiple snapshots that reference overlapping token ranges (cheap merge when base_generation matches).
- If snapshot resolve overhead becomes issue, opportunistically offload resolve work to a lightweight kernel launched earlier (async pre-resolve).

References / links:
- existing paged-KV eviction RFC (internal): confluence://designs/paged-kv-eviction-rfc
- FlashAttention microkernel notes (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/blob/main/notes/flash-kernels.md

Open call: if you care about trying a different snapshot layout (tagged-pairs vs packed-deltas) ping me; I sketched both in the simulator but only implemented packed-deltas so far.

End of doc.
